# 📄 CrewHub (Team Management Web Application) — Requirements Specification

## 1. Overview

The purpose of this application is to provide small teams with a simple platform to:

- [] [] communicate
- [] organise members into teams
- [] schedule and manage events
- [] track basic team activity

The system should be lightweight, intuitive, and accessible via web browsers.

## 2. User Roles

The system shall support the following user roles:

### 2.1 Owner (Team Creator)

- [] Can create and delete teams
- [] Can manage all team settings
- [] Can assign or change user roles
- [] Has full access to all team data

### 2.2 Admin

- [] Can manage team members (invite/remove)
- [] Can create and edit events
- [] Can post in team channels
- [] Cannot delete team or change ownership

### 2.3 Member

- [] Can view team content
- [] Can participate in chat/messages
- [] Can view events and calendar
- [] Cannot manage users or settings

## 3. Core Features

### 3.1 Authentication & Accounts

- [] Users can register and log in securely
- [] Passwords must be securely hashed
- [] Sessions must persist across browser refresh
- [] Users can log out from all devices

### 3.2 Team Management

- [] Users can create a new team
- [] Users can join a team via invite link or code
- [] Teams have unique identifiers
- [] Users can belong to multiple teams

### 3.3 Team Members

- [] View list of team members
- [] Display user role within team
- [] Invite new members via email or shareable link
- [] Remove members (admin+ only)

### 3.4 Messaging System

- [] Each team has a basic message feed or chat
- [] Users can post messages in real time or near-real-time
- [] Messages include:
  - [] author
  - [] timestamp
  - [] content
- [] Basic message history is stored and retrievable

(Note: real-time updates are optional for MVP — polling is acceptable initially)

### 3.5 Events & Scheduling

- [] Teams can create events
- [] Events include:
  - [] title
  - [] description
  - [] date & time
  - [] optional location
- [] Events are visible in a calendar view
- [] Users can view upcoming events by team

### 3.6 Notifications (Optional MVP+)

- [] Notify users of:
  - [] new messages
  - [] new events
  - [] team invites
- [] Notifications may be in-app only for initial version

## 4. Data Requirements

The system must store:

- [] Users
- [] Teams
- [] Memberships (user-role-team relationships)
- [] Messages
- [] Events

Data should be relational and consistent.

## 5. Non-Functional Requirements

### 5.1 Performance

- [] Pages should load within acceptable web standards (<2s typical load time on broadband)
- [] UI should remain responsive under moderate load

### 5.2 Security

- [] Passwords must be hashed (e.g. bcrypt or equivalent)
- [] Protected routes must enforce authentication
- [] Role-based access control must be enforced server-side
- [] Input validation required on all forms
- [] Basic protection against:
- [] XSS
- [] SQL injection
- [] CSRF (if applicable)

### 5.3 Usability

- [] Clean and minimal UI
- [] Mobile responsive design required
- [] Intuitive navigation between teams, chat, and calendar

### 5.4 Reliability

- [] System should handle refresh without data loss
- [] Graceful error handling for API failures

## 6. Technical Constraints

- [] Web-based application only (no native apps required)
- [] Must be deployable using containerisation (Docker)
- [] REST API backend required
- [] Database must persist data reliably (SQL-based preferred)
- [] Frontend must be component-based (e.g. React)

## 7. Suggested Technology Stack (non-mandatory)

- [] Frontend: React + TypeScript
- [] Backend: Node.js (Express/Fastify/NestJS)
- [] Database: PostgreSQL
- [] Caching/offline storage: IndexedDB (optional enhancement)
- [] Deployment: Docker + Docker Compose

## 8. Future Enhancements (Out of Scope for MVP)

- [] Real-time chat (WebSockets)
- [] File sharing
- [] Video calls integration
- [] Advanced analytics dashboard
- [] Mobile application
- [] AI-assisted scheduling

## 9. Acceptance Criteria (MVP)

The project is considered complete when:

- [] Users can register/login/logout
- [] Teams can be created and managed
- [] Roles are enforced correctly
- [] Messages can be posted and retrieved
- [] Events can be created and viewed in calendar form
- [] Application runs locally via Docker setup
- [] Basic documentation is provided
